quote: Okay. I mean, we take care of everything up front for you, so there's nothing out of your pocket.
stewart_read: The customer's 'I don't have any money right now' is a textbook setup for the objection-inversion flip (her financial situation IS the reason to act), but the rep answers it as a logistics question rather than reframing her bill as the actual expense.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's answer is factually correct and does resolve the literal question, so this could be read as adequate handling rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the affordability stall as the entry point for the bill-as-villain flip — e.g. tying her ComEd cost directly to the reason six months of waiting costs her more, not just stating the mechanic is free upfront.

quote: we can't even sell a solar system to anybody unless they're gonna be saving money. So if it's not cheaper than what you're paying now, we can't even sell you a system.
stewart_read: The customer is reciting the program's savings-guarantee logic back to the rep unprompted, which reads as her processing and half-selling herself on the concept rather than a clean buying signal — genuinely ambiguous whether this is enthusiasm or her working through skepticism aloud.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a strong positive buying signal (she's internalizing the pitch), but there isn't enough in the moment itself to confirm that without leaning on the call's later warm ending.
coaching_implication: Flag for the rep to actively engage when the customer parrots program logic back — ask a light follow-up ('exactly right — does that change how you're thinking about it?') to convert the moment into forward motion rather than letting it pass unacknowledged.

quote: Because this has been hot all winter. This is ridiculous.
stewart_read: This unprompted frustration about her bill, volunteered while she's pulling up the actual document, is a stronger and more specific bill-pain anchor than the $150ish number captured earlier, and the rep says nothing in response to it.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to catch live emotional commentary like this and reflect it back ('yeah, that's exactly the kind of spike we're trying to fix') — it's a free, customer-supplied hook that went unused.

quote: Well, I'm going to work. The weekends are better. Friday, Saturday, Sunday on my off day is the best time to talk to.
stewart_read: The customer proactively volunteers her scheduling constraint, and the rep does successfully carry this detail forward to lock Saturday at 2pm later in the call — this is a captured detail feeding the eventual booking, not a miss.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example of information capture and follow-through worth naming to the rep as a repeatable behavior.

quote: Can you send me some information on how it works? Because I'm a little confused.
stewart_read: The rep admits confusion mid-explanation rather than continuing to bluff through the bill-swap mechanic, which is an honest recovery, but it comes after three unclear passes at the same explanation.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as reactive scrambling rather than transparent admission, since it follows repeated unclear answers rather than a single clean moment of honesty.
coaching_implication: Work with the rep on a single, crisp one-sentence description of the bill-swap program to use on the first pass so this admission of confusion isn't needed at all.

quote: You might as well save save some money,
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a closing-adjacent line about paying for solar 'eventually' being the same as her light bill, and the rep's response is a flat generic affirmation rather than reinforcing the specific bill-pain reason she gave earlier ($150+, hot winter).
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to tie the close explicitly back to the customer's own stated numbers and frustration rather than a generic 'save some money' line — reinforcing her own words lands harder than a paraphrase.
